newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan approves construction of two reactors.
newsitem.headline: Japan approves construction of two reactors.

text.p: A Japanese government advisory panel has approved the plans of two regional utility firms to each build an additional nuclear reactor at their plants by 2006, an official for the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.

The approval means the two reactors -- the fifth reactor at Chubu Electric Power Co Inc's Hamaoka plant and the second reactor at Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc's Shika plant -- have officially been integrated into Japan's long-term energy supply plan, he said.
The power firms have already gained the consent of local governments and fisheries groups.

The 1.38 million kilowatt (kw) reactor at the Hamaoka plant on the Pacific coast is scheduled to start commercial operations in August 2005, and the 1.36 kw unit at the Shika plant on the Sea of Japan is expected to begin operations in March 2006.

While the two firms were successful in gaining local support for building additional reactors at their plants, it has become increasingly difficult for the power industry to secure possible sites for new plants due to local opposition.

The public's confidence on the safety of nuclear power plants has been undermined by a series of accidents at nuclear facilities, such as the leakage of sodium coolant at the prototype fast-breeder nuclear reactor Monju in December 1995 and an explosion at a nuclear reprocessing plant earlier this month.
Japan now has 50 commercial reactors, which supply about one-third of domestic electricity, while three others are under construction.
